# Why #26 in white falls on his back after scoring

## Short answer

**He falls because he runs straight into the goalkeeper, who is already lying on the ground in his path.** Nobody tackles him and nobody trips him. He scores, immediately begins celebrating while still sprinting at full speed — head up, mouth open screaming, arm flung up — and his own momentum pitches him forward off his feet into a flat, head-first dive. The Dutch goalkeeper, who had come out and gone to ground when he was beaten, is sprawled directly in front of him. Molina flies into him and lands across his body. The collision stops his lower half while his upper half is still travelling, so he is flipped straight over the top of the keeper, somersaults, and comes to rest flat on his back on the grass — where he lies for about half a second with his fist in the air before rolling over, getting up and sprinting off to celebrate.

## Who and what this is

The video is a FIFA highlights package of **Netherlands vs Argentina, World Cup Qatar 2022 quarter-final**. Argentina wear the white-and-sky-blue striped shirts, the Netherlands wear orange, and the Dutch goalkeeper wears fluorescent green. The player in white with **#26** is Argentina's right-back **Nahuel Molina**; the orange **#4** with the captain's armband running alongside him is **Virgil van Dijk**; the green **#23** is goalkeeper **Andries Noppert**. This is Argentina's opening goal, in the 35th minute (the on-screen clock reads 34:0x), and the scoreboard later shows NED 0–1 ARG.

Two views of the incident exist in the clip:
- the **live main-camera shot at about 0:05.7–0:07.5**, and
- a **slow-motion replay from a low camera behind the byline at about 0:20.4–0:22.2**, which is roughly 2.5× slow motion and shows the mechanics clearly.

## What the frames actually show, in order

1. **He finishes at full sprint.** Molina arrives on the right of the six-yard area at top speed and steers the ball past the goalkeeper with his right foot (live ≈ 0:05.74).

2. **The goalkeeper is beaten and goes to ground immediately.** Within about a tenth of a second of the shot, Noppert has already collapsed to the turf (live ≈ 0:05.82). From this moment on he is a stationary obstacle lying on the grass, roughly two metres ahead of Molina and directly in Molina's running line. **He is not sliding into Molina and he does not tackle him.**

3. **Molina keeps running and starts celebrating at once.** For the next few tenths of a second he is still perfectly upright and sprinting (live ≈ 0:05.86–0:05.98). The close-up replay frames show his mouth wide open shouting and his left arm thrown up and back in celebration while he is still on his feet. He is looking up and ahead, not down at the ground.

4. **He pitches forward off his feet with nobody touching him.** Over about a fifth of a second his torso leans further and further forward, both feet leave the turf, and his legs kick up behind him with the knees bent. In the magnified replay frames there is **visible daylight between Molina and van Dijk throughout this launch** — van Dijk is running alongside on his right with his arms swinging normally, and never pushes him, never puts a leg in, and never trips him. The goalkeeper is still well clear at this instant. So the moment he leaves the ground is caused by his own momentum, not by contact: at a dead sprint, throwing his arms up to celebrate kills the arm-drive that keeps a sprinter balanced, his torso gets ahead of his feet, and he goes over.

5. **He flies into the prone goalkeeper.** He travels roughly horizontally, head first, arms out, and crashes down across Noppert's sprawled body and legs (live ≈ 0:06.14–0:06.22).

6. **The collision flips him onto his back.** Hitting the keeper's body arrests his hips and legs while his head and shoulders are still moving forward, so he tips right over the top of him — he goes over his own shoulder in a somersault, passing from one side of the keeper to the other, and ends up lying flat on his back on the turf beside him (live ≈ 0:06.8–0:07.1).

## Things the video rules out

- **It is not a foul and not a trip by the defender.** Van Dijk is alongside him the whole way and at no point makes contact before Molina leaves the ground. No free kick is given and the goal stands.
- **It is not a goalkeeper's tackle taking his legs.** The keeper is already flat on the ground, beaten, before Molina even begins to lose his balance. The keeper is what Molina lands on, not what knocks him over.
- **It is not an injury.** He is up within about a second and a half.
- **It is not a planned gymnastic celebration.** Landing on his back across a goalkeeper is plainly the accidental outcome of the collision, even though the forward launch itself begins as him celebrating.

## What happens immediately after

He lies on his back for roughly half a second with a fist raised in triumph, rolls over onto his front, pushes himself up onto his feet (live ≈ 0:07.2–0:07.4) and sprints away along the goal line in front of the advertising hoardings, arms outstretched and screaming — the close-up that follows shows him at full pelt with Dutch players flashing past in the foreground. He is completely unhurt, and Argentina lead 1–0.

## One-line summary

He falls on his back because he started celebrating while still running flat out, over-balanced forward off his own feet, and dived head-first straight into the goalkeeper lying on the ground in front of him — and the impact somersaulted him over the top of the keeper and onto his back.
